Show industrial beet-sugar production as a single very clear four-station left-to-right cartoon process. Start with identifiable sliced sugar beet and warm-water extraction in a simple tank; next juice purification with a few precipitated solid particles, then a filter catching those particles, then evaporation and crystallisation in a pan with white sugar crystals. Keep four stations big and uncrowded, joined by unambiguous process arrows. Filtration removes precipitated solids, not dissolved sugar; the dissolved sugar stays in the juice until evaporation/crystallisation. At the bottom, equally prominent simple symbols of leaf/water, coin, and worker convey environmental, economic and social assessment without any winner, approval badge or sustainability guarantee. If labels are used, exactly large German words: 'Extraktion', 'Saftreinigung', 'Filtern', 'Kristallisieren'. No chemical plant maze, no hazardous experiment, no tiny equations. Everything within the canvas.

A clear schematic fat-analysis idea, not a laboratory scene. Large central triacylglyceride schematic: one glycerol backbone with THREE distinct ester bridges connecting THREE long fatty-acid residue chains. For scientifically correct optional condensed structure use vertical glycerol CH2 / CH / CH2 linked respectively through O–C(=O) to R1/R2/R3; each ester carbonyl has its double-bonded O. Or use honest schematic colour-coded bridges rather than an incorrect full formula. Mark the three ester bridges in orange and a few C=C double bonds along the residues in blue. Left large orange counting panel associates ester groups with KOH and the reference mass '1 g Fett'. Right large blue counting panel associates C=C bonds with I2 equivalents and reference mass '100 g Fett'. Major headings exactly 'Verseifungszahl' and 'Iodzahl'. Very short units, if included: 'mg KOH / g Fett' and 'g I₂ / 100 g Fett'. No actual analytical values, no direct iodine student experiment, no health label, no shelf-life clock or unique-composition claim. Make the two counting principles and different reference masses immediately visible; prioritise large simple motifs over text density.

Show catalytic hydrogenation of fat residue chains. In the upper half one very large chemically correct reaction fragment: '–CH=CH– + H₂ → –CH₂–CH₂–' with 'Katalysator' above the reaction arrow. Clearly colour the TWO newly added hydrogen atoms, one on each of the two carbons. The terminal dashes indicate a chain fragment, not a whole triglyceride. Carbon atom count and chain connections unchanged. In the lower half show a few same-length schematic fatty-acid chains, cis-kinked chains with looser packing on the left beside an oil droplet, straighter saturated chains with closer packing on the right beside a small solid-fat block. Short labels 'ungesättigt' and 'gesättigt'. This is a qualitative packing illustration, no guaranteed melting-point number or health ranking. Ester bridges are not cleaved or replaced. No H+ carbocation mechanism, bromine, water formation, laboratory hydrogen equipment, danger scene, photorealism or small text. Large friendly simple shapes.
